qt: to the Commission Christel Schaldemose (S&D) Subject:

Since 1 January 2026, music and singing lessons for adults aged 30 and over have been subject to VAT in Denmark in line with the case-law of the Court of Justice of the European Union. Article 132(1)(i) of the VAT Directive stipulates that the teaching of children and young people can be exempted from VAT where the conditions laid down in the provision concerned are met. Denmark has therefore established that the teaching of people aged 29 and under will continue to be exempt from VAT. This means that older people might have to pay VAT on music and singing lessons, while similar lessons for younger people are exempt. For older people, singing in choirs, for example, can play an important role in social interaction, community and active ageing. With the above in mind: 1.
To what extent does Directive 2006/112/EC allow Member States to exempt from VAT music and singing lessons for older people, including the over-60s?
What is the Commission’s view of the fact that music and singing lessons for younger and older people respectively are treated differently when it comes to VAT?
Will the Commission consider amending or clarifying the VAT rules to give Member States more scope to exempt music and singing lessons for older people from VAT, or apply a reduced rate?
